evidence.note: Explicit numbered build plan (start.sh, app, engine, storage) and dependency-ordered module construction: refs→parser→locale→engine→funcs→controller→store→server→SPA — genuine dependency sequencing, better than a flat list.

Per-layer done-checks embedded in the build: tokenizer verified (16), parser verified (17), FUNCS count checked (35), controller eval smoke-tested (39), server import checked (49) — rough checkpoints tied to quick runnable probes.

All breadth built before ANY test ran (first suite at step 51); dependency-graph/cycle/lambda bugs surfaced only via the smoke suite and were then fixed in a sensible order — the agent did not front-load the highest-risk load-bearing layers or get a core round-trip green before breadth (misses the level-8 anchor).

Post-green adaptive hardening: repeatedly enumerated hidden-test risk areas (persistence, 1k/5k-dependent perf, spill, xlsx round-trip of validations/CF/named ranges) and probed each, re-orienting effort as scope understanding deepened.

reasoning: The agent went well beyond a flat to-do list (level 3): construction was genuinely dependency-ordered with per-layer smoke checkpoints, and a distinct adaptive hardening phase revisited risk areas — matching and exceeding the level-5 'sensible stages with rough checkpoints' description. But it falls short of level 8 because it built the full feature breadth before running any test, rather than front-loading the highest-risk load-bearing layers and getting a live server + persistence + contract-correct core round-trip green first; done-checks emerged from the smoke suite rather than being defined per milestone in advance. This places it at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.
